Process-global cache-clearer registry, the dependency-inversion slot that keeps this gateway off the CloudKitSync/LocalPersistence edge. Concurrency story: HealthKitService is @MainActor, so the static is MainActor-isolated; FernletApp writes it exactly once at launch, before any HealthKitService is constructed, and it is only read afterwards — at init and re-checked at call time in disableIntegration(), which throws cacheClearerUnavailable when it is still nil, so a disable can never silently skip the purge of cached clinical values.

CryptoKit seam — the ONE byte-export of a SymmetricKey in the shipping tree, `SymmetricKey.rawBytes` at the bottom of this file. SymmetricKey is not a Sequence and exposes its material only through ContiguousBytes.withUnsafeBytes; there is no Data(key) initializer or other byte accessor. Invariant: the closure copies the borrowed buffer into an owned Data INSIDE the callback, so no pointer, buffer, or index escapes withUnsafeBytes and the buffer is never read after it returns. PendingNarrativeBuffer, PrivateMediaKeyStore and this file's loadOrCreateSymmetricKey all call rawBytes now, which is why they no longer need entries of their own; narrowed by line_contains so any other unsafe construct added to this file stays enforced.

SQLite C-API seam: the cast reproduces the SQLITE_TRANSIENT macro ((sqlite3_destructor_type)-1), a C macro Swift cannot import. SQLite compares the value by identity to mean 'copy the bound text now' and never invokes or dereferences it; the alternative (nil = SQLITE_STATIC) would require the Swift String's storage to outlive the statement.

Security-framework seam: SecAccessControlCreateWithFlags reports failure through a Create-rule CFError out-parameter that Swift imports as Unmanaged<CFError>?. In KeychainItem.accessControl(for:) the value is consumed exactly once via takeRetainedValue() on the failure path (balancing the +1 retain) to throw the real error, is never stored or escaped, and the success path never touches it. Narrowed by line_contains so every other unsafe construct in this file stays enforced.

Security-framework seam: SecKeyCreateDecryptedData reports failure through a Create-rule CFError out-parameter imported as Unmanaged<CFError>?. This is the ONE site in the file that needs it — unwrapResult consumes it exactly once via takeRetainedValue() immediately after the call, to tell a transient failure (interaction-not-allowed / not-available / auth-failed / user-canceled) apart from a terminal one, and never stores or escapes it. Core Data seam: `NSPersistentContainer` is not `Sendable`, so the process-wide sealed-store controller cannot be a checked-Sendable global, and real actor isolation is unavailable because all four sealed repositories are deliberately `nonisolated` so keyless deletion works from any executor while the app is locked. Invariant: `shared` is a `let` initialized exactly once by Swift's lazy-static machinery; every use of `container.viewContext` happens inside `NSManagedObjectContext.performAndWait`, which serializes on the context's own queue; and the one piece of mutable state outside that discipline, `didFailToLoad`, is now read and written only under the type's `stateLock` (`NSLock`).

Exercise-animation raster seam: the approved renderer's per-pixel triangle and capsule loops write the 640 x 480 colour and Float32 depth buffers. Through Array subscripts an unoptimised (Debug) build paid a generic call per element and a frame took 100-450 ms; pointer subscripts are transparent, so the same loops take 7-19 ms with bit-identical output. Invariant: triangle(_:) and segment(_:) first guard that both arrays hold exactly width*height elements and that the job's clamped column/row ranges lie inside the canvas; the base addresses are used only inside the nested with... closures (passed to triangleRows/segmentRows, which never store them), and every index is row*640 + column with row and column inside those ranges. The arrays are the raster's own stored properties, borrowed as two distinct inout stored properties, so nothing else can observe the writes.

Exercise-animation raster seam: the parameter types of triangleRows/segmentRows, which receive the base addresses borrowed in triangle(_:)/segment(_:) (see this file's withUnsafeMutableBufferPointer entry). They are called only from inside those closures, never store or return the pointers, and index only row*640 + column for the job's canvas-clamped rows and columns, after the caller has checked both buffers hold exactly 640*480 elements.

Exercise-animation image seam: hands the finished frame to CGDataProvider as Data. The closure copies the borrowed bytes of the [UInt32] pixel array (0xAABBGGRR values, which little-endian are the canvas's R,G,B,A bytes) into an owned Data INSIDE the callback, so no pointer or buffer escapes withUnsafeBytes; the copy is one memcpy where a per-byte Swift loop cost about 50 ms per frame in a Debug build.
